changes_made.explanation: Normalized dataset name to 'RuleArena' (proper capitalization), normalized model names with hyphen formatting, simplified output descriptions while maintaining their core meaning, removed redundant task entry

Simplified to base metric names rather than specific formula variants (R(t), AC(t), etc.). The paper uses classic metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall) with rule-specific variations, but the core metrics are these standard ones.
Kept GPT-4o as the LLM judge, simplified method descriptions, and clarified evaluation criteria to focus on core aspects mentioned in the paper
No human evaluation was conducted according to the paper text. The evaluation relied on automatic metrics and LLM-based parsing.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating LLMs' ability to follow complex natural language rules across three domains (airline luggage fees, NBA transactions, tax calculations). While it evaluates generated outputs (calculated answers and decisions), these are more reasoning/computation outputs than traditional NLG. The extraction quality was good overall, requiring mainly normalization and simplification of metric names. The paper uses GPT-4o as an LLM judge to parse and analyze the rule application in model responses.
